post.title: Why 'Don't' Makes You Want It More #shorts
post.description: Would you open it? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who hears 'don't' as 'do'. Theo leaves a box with a note: DON'T OPEN. Milo says he doesn't care, then stares at it for ten minutes. Psychologist Jack Brehm called it reactance (A Theory of Psychological Reactance, 1966): when a freedom is threatened, we want it back. In 1976 James Pennebaker and Deborah Sanders (Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 'American Graffiti: Effects of Authority and Reactance Arousal') put signs banning graffiti in toilet stalls: the stronger the threat and the higher the authority behind it, the more graffiti ended up on the signs themselves. The box wasn't interesting. The rule was. #psychology #shorts #reactance #overthinking #relatable
